source: PC NFH2, the anger gauge's jumps in Badinfos' 100 % run (tools/pcref/amounts.py: the jump per second scaled to the full bar, 92 % of the crop, labelled with the HUD bubble's activity) — a jump that hits the full bar is a lower bound and keeps the mobile value where that is higher; a jump shared by linked coins is split in the mobile proportions; an unmeasured coin keeps the mobile value. E02 Covert Advance: +19 the rake (96 s), +25 the swim (105), +45 in the swim — the submarine (116), +25 the rail and +10 at the full bar its pond (148-150); the mat's coin shows no jump. PC data (cn_b1/tricks.xml, rage per trick in thousandths of the gauge): the PC differs from the mobile on Rake 20 (rake_ground), Submarine 35 (shark), EelBox 30 (bridge_electrify); the rest are equal. The gauge jumps read off Badinfos' video (2026-09-08) ran 10-25 %% high and are withdrawn. The gauge is 100 000 rage long — the mobile's AngryMeterMaximum 100: the PC dialog (nfh2 dialogs/*/menuleft_bar.xml) gives the rageometer range 0..100000 and GameLogic.dll flags 100000 (docs/PC_ROUTINES.md); the 80 read off the video was the bar's geometry, as the Season 1 tube's was. Its decay is the mobile's 0.37 %/s: the bar falls 41 -> 11 % over 70 trick-free seconds of E01 (tools/pcref/gauge.py, x0.8 for the crop). The decay is leveldata.xml's time="30" per 1/12 s tick (GameLogic.dll fcn.10044234: rage -= the level record's +0x28, the app's leveldata parser stores `time` there; the HUD clock divides the tick count by 12) — PCRageDecay 30, 0.36 %/s against the mobile's 0.37.

patches.note: the rake's component is the Rake subclass (scene.py), not a plain TrickItem — the patch matched nothing until 2026-09-17
cn_b1/tricks.xml shark=35000: the coin is read from the Swimming item's AngerAmount when the shark pays, not from the Submarine that arms it (2026-09-17)
